description:
FILED s431 (Opus 5), minimised from the module-population census (#462, docs/drop-census-s431-flip-gate.md section 5).

REPRODUCERS (perl prints ok in every row; PCL announces a drop and continues):

    my $m = "strict.pm"; require $m if 1;                    DROP
    my $m = "strict.pm"; require $m unless $INC{$m};         DROP
    local($\, $,) = (undef, "") if 1;                        DROP

    my $m = "strict.pm"; require $m;                         ok   <- no modifier
    my $m = "strict.pm"; if (1) { require $m }               ok   <- block form
    require strict if 1;                                     ok   <- BAREWORD argument
    local($\, $,) = (undef, "");                             ok   <- no modifier
    our @a; local (@a) = (1,2) if 1;                         ok   <- container
    our $p; local $p = 1 if 1;                               ok   <- single scalar

So the trigger is the MODIFIER combined with a statement class the lowerer
handles specially: `require` with a SCALAR argument, and a `local` LIST
assignment.  The announcement shows the statement text starting mid-statement
(`$m if delete $INC{$m}`), i.e. the modifier path re-lowers the inner statement
through a route that has no case for these classes.  Suspect ONE cause; probe
before assuming two.

WHERE IT BITES: 4 of Test-Simple's 15 module drops (`require ... unless
$INC{...}` in Test2::API::Context, Test2::API::InterceptResult(::Event) x2) and
Sub::Uplevel line 49 (`require $m if delete $INC{$m}`, a board dist).  Both are
SILENT today (module mode announces nothing), and the effect is a module that
silently does not reload.

BAR: the nine rows above vs perl; the modifier family in both directions
(`unless`, `while`, `for`); corpus-diff; a Pl/t guard row; then re-run the
module census (#462) and count the drops that leave.


DONE s441b (Opus agent B; merged by Fable s440 as b81142b). ONE cause, as suspected: the modifier split lived inside _process_expression_statement, so every per-class handler that slices tokens by position handed the modifier to _parse_expression. Two shared halves in Pl/Parser.pm, one copy each -- _split_trailing_modifier(\@parts, $accept) (the caller declares which of the six words it can lower; a word outside the set reads as "no modifier", which is why `local ... for (1,2)` keeps dropping LOUDLY instead of becoming a silent wrong -- perl restores it per iteration, probed) and _wrap_statement_modifier (the p-if/p-unless/p-while/p-until/p-foreach generation, moved out unchanged). Four callers: the expression statement (unchanged), the require-EXPRESSION branch (all six modifiers), the multi-var `local(LIST)=RHS` branch (if/unless), and `local *glob = RHS if C` whose inline fourth copy is deleted. `local(LIST)=RHS if C` also needed a shape: the condition once into pcl-local-cond-N (first binding, before the RHS), `(if COND rhs nil)` for the RHS, each slot bound to a COPY OF ITS CURRENT VALUE, `(when COND (p-list-= ...))` for the assignment. `require "literal" if C` stops taking the compile-time p-eval-always reading. Measured vs caa3d07: corpus-diff IDENTICAL (111, drops 5), lib A/B SAME=22, perl-t A/B SAME=528, cpan A/B 402 with exactly the four carrying files DIFF, RCDIFF=0. Census 80/183 -> 76/174 (then recounted at the merge with agent A: 73/167). Guard Pl/t/stmt-modifier-01.t (12 rows; every program re-run under real perl; one row asserts the loop-modifier drop is still loud, one that `local *glob = RHS if C` still lowers); inverse-run on the base parser = 22 failures. Gate 169/5801 PASS. NOT fixed, FILED: #508 bare `local $x if 0` ignores the modifier; #509 an element/slice target in a local LIST is never assigned; #510 `$!` in a local LIST is never assigned; #511 %INC not populated by a bareword require/use. Also found: #457's board row was already zero on main.
subject: DONE s441b: A STATEMENT MODIFIER on two statement classes DROPS the whole statement: `require $m if COND;` and `local($\, $,) = (undef,'') if COND;` (both fine without the modifier) -- 5 of the 20 module-population drops
